title: Persistent labels, useful hints, explicit optionality
summary: Give controls persistent labels, add concise hints only when they help answer correctly, and identify optional information explicitly.
problem: Placeholder-only or vague form controls force users to remember context after typing and make requirements difficult to understand.
use_when: Collecting user input with text fields, choices, dates, uploads, or other controls
A field has format, purpose, or optionality users may not infer
avoid_when: A hint merely repeats the label or adds no useful information
rationale: Useful hints prevent errors better than corrective messages after submission.

prefer_alternatives_if: The control's accessible name and visible context are already explicit and no hint is needed
use_if: Collecting user input with text fields, choices, dates, uploads, or other controls
A field has format, purpose, or optionality users may not infer

requirements: Every control needs a persistent accessible name.
Associate hints and errors programmatically with their control.
Do not encode required/optional state with color or punctuation alone.
Use labels that describe requested information, not implementation terms.
Keep examples out of placeholders when they must remain visible after entry.
